newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair CEO says 96/97 op earnings fell.
newsitem.headline: Finnair CEO says 96/97 op earnings fell.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy's CEO Antti Potila said in a company newsletter received on Wednesday that the group's 1996/97 operating earnings to end-March were clearly weaker than in 1995/96.
"We have already seen for a long time that the result of operations for the financial year now ended will be clearly weaker than the previous year," Potila said.

In the year to end-March 1996, the group's operating profit was 624 million markka. Releasing in November its first-half to end-September results, Finnair said it expected 1996/97 operating profit to be clearly below 1995/96.
"Although we can be satisfied in many ways with the financial year ended, the earnings trend of the year was not at all satisfactory," Potila said.
Looking ahead, Potila said competition for passengers and market share would be tight. "This will mark operations in our new financial year," he said.
"Demand for air travel is rising in line with the economic recovery," Potila said, adding this would create pressures to take on new staff.
"But considering the profitability trend we must be exceptionally strict in this respect," he said. @
